fantasy: You are the paddle in a pop-up book: one bright ball, one finger, and a paper world of bricks that crumples into confetti, rebound by rebound, until the boss folds flat.
core_loop: Launch the ball -> drag the paddle to angle rebounds off the paddle and the side walls -> break bricks and catch the power-ups they drop (multi-ball, a wide paddle on a timer, a laser that lets the paddle shoot) -> clear the board for up to three stars -> stars open the next level and each world's star gate -> replay a level for the stars you missed; 32 hand-built levels in 4 worlds of 8, each world adding its own brick type or hazard (armored two-hit bricks, unbreakable steel bricks with sliding rows, a descending field, explosive bricks and falling embers) and ending in a boss level with a health bar.
pillars: One finger, one paddle: the player can always read where the ball will go next
Every brick is a small crunch you see and hear; every boss hit is a bigger one
Four paper worlds, one new trick each, and back in a level within one second of a miss

engine.rationale: Ball-and-brick play happens on a flat plane and needs no depth to read; 2D with procedural vector paper-cut art and a hand-written circle-vs-rectangle reflection keeps the first load small on portal traffic, where time to first play decides whether the player stays, and holds 30 fps on a mid-range phone.
engine.camera: Fixed portrait playfield: bricks in the upper two thirds, the paddle on a rail near the bottom, no scrolling; the descending field moves the brick layer, never the camera.

features.name: Drag the paddle
features.description: The paddle follows the player's finger or pointer along a rail near the bottom of the field; the ball leaves it at an angle set by where it struck.
acceptance: The paddle's x equals the pointer's x (clamped to the walls) within one frame; it never moves vertically.

scope.progression_terminal: Progression ends at the world 4 boss: 32 levels in 4 worlds of 8, 96 stars. After it the player replays levels for stars and best scores, and plays Endless Rally, which reuses authored rows; there is no content treadmill to feed.

session.structure: A level lasts 15 to 60 s. A session is 5 to 8 levels back to back: the first session drops straight into level 1 with no menu and a first brick breaks within 8 s; later sessions open on the title and the level map. Each win lands on the map with the next level lit, each fail restarts the level within a second, and the session ends on a boss, a star gate or a new best rather than being cut off.
session.end_condition: The player clears a boss or a star gate opens, or two attempts in a row fail on the same level and they leave from the result card.

retention.return_reason: I am three stars short of opening the Foundry gate, and I know exactly which level I lost a ball on.
retention.progression_loop: Clear a level -> earn up to three stars -> the next level opens and stars add up toward each world's star gate (12, 28, 44) -> replay a level for the stars and best score you missed -> beat the world boss -> after world 4, Endless Rally.

placements.trigger: When the last ball is lost after at least 15 s of play on that attempt, offer one extra ball per attempt
placements.player_value: A fresh ball on the paddle; every brick already broken stays broken

placements.trigger: When the player leaves the level-complete card, at most once every 180s, never after the first level of a session and never inside play
placements.player_value: None - a pure interruption at a natural break, priced as such and held to the tightest platform cadence

monetization.economy: No currency. Stars are earned only by play; the rewarded extra ball is the only economic action.

progression: Skill only: clear level n -> level n + 1 opens; 12 stars -> world 2 (Clockwork Foundry) opens; 28 stars -> world 3 (Frostline) opens; 44 stars -> world 4 (Ember Peak) opens; clear the world 4 boss -> Endless Rally opens.
difficulty: Authored per level on speed, density, variety and precision. World 1 (levels 1-8) teaches the drag, capsules, armored bricks and a first health bar; world 2 adds steel and sliding rows, world 3 the descending field, world 4 explosive bricks and falling embers, each world opening on an easier level that introduces its new piece and closing on a boss that combines it with everything before. Assist: after three failed attempts on one level, the next attempt starts with a fourth ball.
controls: Move the paddle: press and drag in the lower half of the screen (touch), move the pointer (mouse), Left/Right or A/D (keyboard). Launch: the first press, click or Space; the ball also launches itself after 3 s. Pause: Pause button, Esc or P.

ux.onboarding: Diegetic. A ghost hand slides the paddle under the ball on the first frame of level 1, the ball launches into a single row of bricks, and the first brick break teaches the rest; no text beyond one objective line.
ux.accessibility: Every audio cue has a visual counterpart, so the game plays muted - which also covers the large share of portal traffic that plays with sound off. Colour is never the only signal. Text is at least 16 CSS px at the design resolution. A reduced-motion setting (and prefers-reduced-motion) disables shake and flashes.

art_direction: Identity kit 'paper-diorama', chosen because the game is four themed worlds and a brick wall is already a stack of cut paper: every world is a layered paper diorama (meadow, foundry, frostline, ember peak) lit from the upper left, each layer casting a short hard shadow down-right. Bricks are ink-outlined paper tiles with one fold line, the ball is a marigold paper disc, the paddle a cream paper tab, and bosses are large multi-layer paper sculptures that tear and fold flat when beaten. The backdrop sits low in contrast so the ball, paddle and bricks lead; UI panels are paper cards with irregular cut edges and marigold tab buttons.
audio_direction: Library music loops (a bright title loop, a play loop, a heavier boss loop) plus short library SFX, all compressed and loaded after first play so audio never delays time to first play. Brick breaks rise in pitch with each brick broken between paddle touches; every cue has a visual twin so the game plays muted.

mechanics.description: The paddle follows the player's finger or pointer along a rail near the bottom of the field.

mechanics.name: Launch and rebound
mechanics.description: The ball rests on the paddle, launches on the first press, and reflects off the paddle, side walls, ceiling and bricks.
rules: The ball launches on the first press, or by itself after 3 s, and keeps the level's ball speed after every bounce.
Walls and the ceiling reflect the ball exactly; the ball never travels flatter than 15 degrees from horizontal.
Ball speed in px/s is 320 + 700 x the level's speed value, and a ball that passes the paddle line is lost.

mechanics.name: Break the bricks
mechanics.description: Bricks break when the ball hits them; breaking every breakable brick wins the level.
rules: A standard brick breaks on the first hit and scores 10; an armored brick takes two hits and scores 20.
The bricks-left counter falls on every break and the level is won on the frame it reaches 0.
Unbreakable steel bricks never count toward bricks left.

mechanics.name: Three balls per attempt
mechanics.description: Each attempt starts with 3 balls; losing the last ball ends the attempt.
rules: A lost ball is replaced by a fresh ball resting on the paddle within 0.6 s while the supply is above 0.
Extra balls from multi-ball do not count toward the supply; only losing the last ball in play costs one.
A new attempt always restores the level's bricks and 3 balls (4 after the assist).

mechanics.name: Catch power-up capsules
mechanics.description: Gold-cornered bricks drop a capsule that falls toward the paddle; catching it applies multi-ball, a wide paddle or a laser that lets the paddle shoot bolts at the bricks.
rules: A capsule falls at 180 px/s and is applied the frame it touches the paddle; one that passes the paddle is gone.

Multi-ball splits the ball into 3 fanned 20 degrees apart; wide paddle grows the paddle from 120 to 180 px for 12 s; laser fires one bolt every 0.5 s for 8 s, each bolt dealing one hit to the first brick it meets and stopping at steel.
Each capsule carries its own glyph (three dots, double arrow, bolt) readable at 48 px.

mechanics.name: Stars per level
mechanics.description: A cleared level awards up to three stars: one for clearing, one for losing no ball, one for beating its par time. Stars measure the player against each world's star gate, and a locked level or world stays locked until the gate is met.
rules: Star 1 is awarded on a win, star 2 only if no ball was lost in the attempt, star 3 only if the win came in under the level's par_s seconds.
A level keeps its best star count; the star total is the sum of the per-level bests.
Gate: the star total is measured against each world's star gate (12, 28, 44); the gate opens on the frame the total reaches it.
Lock: a level is locked until the level before it is cleared, and a world is locked until its gate is met; locked nodes show a lock icon and cannot be entered.

mechanics.name: Boss with a health bar
mechanics.description: A boss level is won by emptying the boss's health bar with ball hits on its weak point, once the shield bricks around it are broken.
rules: The health bar is shown from the first frame and loses one pip per ball hit on the weak point; a hit on a shield or elsewhere on the body scores but deals no damage.
The weak point is covered until its shield bricks are broken, flashes marigold when open, and the boss drops a capsule at set health thresholds.
At half health the boss moves faster; the boss's movement never leaves the field.

elements.description: A paper brick that breaks on the first hit and is the bulk of every wall.
A clay brick that cracks on the first hit and breaks on the second, so the ball must come back to it.
A riveted steel brick that never breaks and does not count as a brick left: the player aims around it and its bars shape the channels.
A row of bricks that slides side to side and wraps at the walls, so the gaps to the back rows open and close on a beat.
The whole wall creeps down a step every few seconds; if it touches the paddle line the attempt is lost, so the player must clear in time.
A firecracker brick that blows up its eight neighbours when broken and chains into other firecrackers, so one hit can clear a cluster.
An ember that drops from the top; if it touches the paddle it burns the paddle narrow for 3 s and ends any capsule effect, so the player must dodge while aiming.
A capsule that splits the ball into three, so the player tracks several rebounds at once.
A capsule that widens the paddle by half for 12 s, forgiving aim for a while.
A capsule that lets the paddle fire a bolt every half second for 8 s, reaching bricks the ball cannot.

open_questions: The design is the brick-breaker the brief and the strategy describe (paddle, ball, bricks, three power-ups, four worlds of eight levels with bosses); the starting draft's drop-merge archetype was discarded. Confirm at G3 that the loop is the one the strategy meant.

The brief asks for an endless mode and the commitments require one, but the strategy's out-of-scope list excludes 'a second mode' beyond the content budget; Endless Rally is included as a post-mvp replay of authored rows that adds no unit, element or mechanic. Confirm at G3 that this reading is accepted.

Levels w1-l3, w1-l5, w1-l7 and the other 'collect' levels end when the capsule quota is caught and the board is cleared, with spare gold bricks re-dropping missed capsules; the prototype should confirm that a missed capsule never leaves a level unwinnable.
A first-time player understands the drag control without instruction
The core loop produces an unforced desire to retry within one 300-second session

Yandex Games is the required platform and CrazyGames and Y8 ship from the same build; confirm in the prototype that one build passes all three SDK adapters and that the 60 s Yandex and 180 s CrazyGames/Y8 interstitial cadences are both honoured by the strictest-interval service.
The rewarded placement reads as a favour rather than an interruption
It holds 30 fps on a mid-range mobile browser inside a 100 MB bundle

Depth the strategy excludes is not built: no currency, shop, cosmetics, daily rewards, missions or leaderboard; stars, star gates and best scores carry the return loop. A superseding strategy admits more, or production adds it after G4.
